call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer:
Systemic innovative solutions that make ports greener, more circular and more resilient, demonstrated in at least four ports in four European basins.
The topic serves the EU Mission Restore our Ocean and Waters (an EU programme with 2030 targets for healthy seas and waters). Solutions should reduce pollution and environmental degradation, reverse biodiversity loss and improve resource management in port areas, in coastal and inland ports of any type and size.
Projects should cover five activity lines, with demonstrations in four ports and work with four associated regions; the call names no excluded activities.
- Test, deploy and upscale innovative solutions to restore port ecosystems and mitigate pollution for one or more Mission objectives, and monitor their effectiveness
- Bring together ports, local stakeholders, authorities, science and industry to develop local Implementation Strategies, for example on renewable energy, alternative fuels, circular economy, biodiversity restoration and nature-based solutions, or adaptation to sea-level rise and extreme weather
- Share knowledge within and between ports and demonstrate transferability and scalability
- Provide assistance and capacity building to smaller ports, for example waste management systems or vegetated buffers protecting port infrastructure
- Create synergies with other EU, national and regional programmes and leverage funding from authorities, the private sector and investors
Demonstrations take place in at least 4 ports, one in each basin: Atlantic and Arctic; Mediterranean; Baltic and North Sea; Danube including the Black Sea.
Need: Ports pollute and degrade marine and freshwater ecosystems and are exposed to climate risks; they need help to act on the Mission's 2030 targets.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Expected Outcome and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all outcomes: measurable progress on Mission targets, ports ready to deploy solutions, more ports acting, more resilience, and knowledge sharing.
- Measurable, quantifiable, verifiable and ambitious progress towards one or more interlinked Mission objectives and targets by 2030, through place-based and people-centred actions
- Ports and port cities involved and ready to test, deploy and upscale systemic solutions, including monitoring invasive species and improving ecosystem connectivity
- More ports taking concrete measures to protect ecosystems and biodiversity, eliminate pollution and make the blue economy carbon-neutral and circular
- More resilience to extreme climate events, sea-level rise, floods and droughts, especially through less pollution and better environmental management
- Better knowledge sharing within and across ports and their communities
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Expected Outcome

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer:
Consortia of ports, port authorities, local stakeholders, science and industry, with demonstrations in four ports in four basins; there is no prescribed lead.
- Lead: any beneficiary may coordinate; the call reserves the role for no organisation type
- Composition: the general rule requires three independent legal entities from three countries; public bodies managing ports and their communities are strongly encouraged as partners, with strong involvement of public administrations and port managing authorities
- Sites: at least 4 ports, one in each of the Atlantic and Arctic, Mediterranean, Baltic and North Sea, and Danube and Black Sea basins
- Work split: none prescribed; cascade grants of up to EUR 100,000 may go only to local or regional public authorities not already at a demonstration site
- Exclusion: legal entities established in China are not eligible for innovation actions
The call suits port authorities, port cities, environmental technology and nature-based-solution companies, waste and water specialists and marine research institutes.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Specific conditions, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer:
The project must test, deploy and upscale innovative solutions, and may build on the best available knowledge from earlier projects.
A systemic combination of technology, nature-based solutions, governance and cooperation models between ports and authorities.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 6–8 by the end of the project.
TRL 6 is technology demonstrated in a relevant environment; TRL 8 is a complete and qualified system.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer:
Demonstration in real ports is required: at least 4, one in each of the four sea and river basins.
Demonstrations need strong involvement of public administrations and port managing authorities; existing activities in some ports can serve as pilots that other ports learn from.
The solutions must be systemic and fit local Implementation Strategies that bring together ports, authorities, science and industry.

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer:
The call touches TenneT's field only narrowly: port energy strategies may include renewable energy and electrification, which depend on grid connections in Dutch ports.
This is our interpretation. One example of a local Implementation Strategy is the transition to renewable energy and alternative fuels, and ports are hubs for offshore wind landing and industrial electrification planned in TenneT's Onshore and Offshore Grid Investment Plans 2026. Environmental improvements in ports could also ease public support for energy infrastructure there. TenneT cannot usefully take part: the call funds port ecology, pollution and resilience measures led by ports and authorities, and sets out no role for a transmission system operator.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
About 2 projects of EUR 5.5–5.95 million each are expected, within a topic budget of EUR 11.9 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: EUR 5.5–5.95 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: actual-cost grant with a 25% flat rate for indirect costs, part of which may be passed on as cascade grants of up to EUR 100,000
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 25–26 · Call HORIZON-MISS-2027-03, Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 131–134 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-03-OCEAN-03, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — Budget flexibility

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
Authorities are encouraged to combine other funds, such as regional development funds or LIFE, to deploy solutions.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant reimburses only eligible costs actually incurred, plus a flat 25% for indirect costs; subcontracting should stay a limited part.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting and purchase costs (equipment, travel, other goods and services), plus personnel unit costs where the beneficiary uses them
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are a flat rate of 25% of eligible direct costs, excluding subcontracting and financial support to third parties
- Subcontracting or equipment: subcontracting should normally be a limited part of the project and be done by third parties, not by beneficiaries; purchases must give best value for money
Budgeted costs are not paid as such: only the costs actually incurred are reimbursed.
- Caps: cascade grants only as grants, only to local or regional public authorities not already at a demonstration site, at most EUR 100,000 each and once per recipient
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 21 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 21 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 40 pages
- Opening: 9 February 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 25–26 · Call HORIZON-MISS-2027-03, Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around February 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 40 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
cards.sources:

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Four ports in four basins, four associated regions and the rules for cascade grants to authorities shape every proposal.
- Conditional — demonstrations: at least 4 ports, one per basin
- Conditional — associated regions: at least 4, with outreach, knowledge sharing, technical assistance and replication plans
- Conditional — cascade grants: if used, only to eligible public authorities, up to EUR 100,000 and once each
- Recommended: public bodies managing ports as partners; combine other funds; build on earlier projects
